proposal.summary: Refine discovery deduplication and the existing evidence-recovery skill. Retain fetch-failure guidance; the run demonstrated successful recovery rather than consistently bad outcomes.

edits.title: Inspect results and resolve aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, handle each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier empty event. Compare entity identities rather than exact name strings: punctuation variants, omitted initials, and contextually established surname-only mentions of known entities are aliases, not new discoveries. Preserve observed spellings in an alias map without merging ambiguous names. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including productive searches that verify missing fields for known entities; do not invent discoveries to suppress a stall warning.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered evidence
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific unresolved fields. Review saved responses first: an extraction may leave a field empty despite available evidence. Track semantic incompleteness as well as empty values; a matching quotation or nonempty cell does not establish complete scope, correct entity attribution, or the required time period. Request concise factual summaries for missing fields and brief supporting excerpts where needed, rather than full-page reproduction. Test a revised focus on one usable page before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus rather than overwriting earlier evidence. For genuinely absent information, use alternative sources instead of inferring from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. When exact wording is required, obtain the complete supported phrase rather than treating a summary or fragment as complete. Keep research-status notes outside factual values. Validate quotations against an individual saved response, then review their support for the entity, field, scope, and relevant time. Supply reviewers the actual contract, including whether quotations must match rendered text or original source text and which fields require historical timing. Repair concrete defects, revalidate changed cells, and stop when no concrete gaps remain. A FETCH_FAILED response calls for bounded retries and source switching, not this incomplete-response procedure.

additional_candidates.description: Exact-string novelty checks counted spelling variants and surname-only mentions as newly discovered entities.
Reviewing populated cells and saved evidence recovered omitted fields, incomplete motivations, and attribution problems that quote-membership checks did not detect.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern verification of already discovered entities: six year-level nationality searches, three targeted affiliation/nationality searches, four person-level nationality searches, and three final audit searches. Their empty discovery records are consistent with no new entities, while subsequent retrieval supplied useful missing evidence. The existing memory already permits honest empty records for verification searches. Repeated signals in its outcome history therefore do not establish consistently bad behavior or justify suppressing them. Alias overcounting is addressed separately.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel-domain requests, two early alternative-domain requests, five later gap-filling requests, two Genzel sources, and two final Nature sources. The agent reused saved hits, tested a small fallback batch, excluded attempted URLs, and recovered through usable alternative sources, including a CV and a professional-society announcement. Existing memory already covers this procedure and correctly avoids attributing failures to URL suffixes. The outcome histories contain repeated failures but passing checks; this trajectory demonstrates recovery under that guidance, not evidence for deleting it or adding a permanent domain blacklist.

The discovery log records omitted initials, alternate apostrophes, and later surname-only mentions as new entities after their full names were already discovered. The trajectory uses exact string membership in known_names, explaining the inflated novelty. Final rows remained unique, so this is a recovered bookkeeping failure rather than a demonstrated output duplication. Extend the existing discovery memory with identity-aware alias handling.

Quote checks repeatedly passed while a motivation remained a fragment, later with an editorial note, and some supported cells stayed empty. Evidence reviews identified these problems and misleading shared-recipient framing; targeted retrieval and repairs resolved them before the final review and deterministic checks passed. Reviewers also raised original-page quotation concerns until the rendered-text contract was clarified. Extend the existing recovery skill with this successful audit-and-repair procedure. Its empty usage/outcome history does not support deletion or claims of prior failure.
